pr_title: catalog: break dependency on eval package
pr_body:
This dependency was introduced because virtual tables need to have privilege descriptors synthesized for them instead of having them provided by the table descriptor.

This commit refactors the privilege descriptor retrieval logic to break this dependency. No functionality should be altered.

Fixes #88400.

Release note: None
pr_comments: @ajwerner is this enough to declare victory for #88400? I'm guessing not, but I'm also unsure about what remains to be done and how urgent it is. I just want to get rid of the existing `PrivilegeObject` interface with the `eval.Planner` dependency.
This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/92601)

> could add the package here to prevent a regression

Thanks! Done.

Thanks for the reviews!

issue_context.title: catalog: break `eval` dependency
issue_context.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

The introduction of virtual privileges brought with it a dependency between `sql/catalog` and `sql/sem/eval` which is far from necessary. The reason it exists is to synthesize a privilege descriptor for virtual tables. We could do that in the descs collection itself when resolving virtual tables. In fact, it'd be much cleaner if we did.

The other two uses of the `GetPrivilegeDescriptor` method are the `GlobalPrivileges` and the `ExternalConnectionPrivileges`. Whenever either is used, we have the things we need on hand to resolve that into a `PrivilegeDescriptor` and thus `catalog.PrivilegeObject` eagerly as opposed to delaying the call into `CheckUserPrivilege`.


Jira issue: CRDB-19802

review_comments: I don't get it, what now looks up the privileges?
It's still the planner, just without the indirection via the `eval.Planner` interface. See `grant_revoke_system.go`.
